item.title: Ranji Trophy: Karnataka fail to seize the moment against Tripura
item.description: MYSURU: Exploiting an opponent’s weakness is par for the course in sport. Karnataka were expected to do just that against Tripura, but have missed a trick or two. After letting the visitors off the hook on the opening day of their Ranji Trophy Group B match at the SDNRW Ground here, the hosts failed to make the most of promising starts on Tuesday, leaving themselves with plenty of work to do despite securing their first innings lead of the season. At stumps, Karnataka were 297/7, ahead by 103 runs. In normal circumstances, three points from a drawn game could have been acceptable. But, as head coach R Vinay Kumar pointed out, this is a must-win match. With just two points from as many games, Karnataka need a victory to keep their knockout hopes alive. In a game of fine margins, Karnataka have been struggling to get ahead. Tuesday was another case in point. Against a bowling attack that was, at best, ordinary, the hosts had an opportunity to build a substantial lead, with both young batters keen to make a mark and seasoned campaigners at the crease. Instead, they scored at just 3.2 runs an over and lost wickets at regular intervals on a surface where the odd ball kept low. Resuming at 10/1, rookie Rohan Patil (72; 130b, 9x4) and Vyshak Vijaykumar adopted a cautious approach and nearly saw off the first hour. However, Vyshak fell while attempting to drive a fuller delivery from Sandeep Sarkar, edging it to wicketkeeper Sentu Sarkar. Karnataka had managed just 36 runs by the 20th over. Rohan and KV Aneesh (68; 142b, 6x4) then added 82 for the third wicket, showing patience against the Tripura attack, which didn’t command that kind of an approach. Rohan, known more as a big-hitting white-ball specialist, brought up his maiden first-class half-century off 88 balls with a back-foot punch through the covers. His promising knock ended when he attempted to flick a fuller delivery from Abhijith Sarkar (3/59) and was trapped leg-before. The arrival of seasoned campaigner Karun Nair (68; 85b, 8x4) injected urgency into the innings, his fluent strokeplay unsettling the bowlers. Dropped on 11 by wicketkeeper Sentu off Bikram Debnath, Karun made the most of the reprieve before Sandip Sarkar (2/83) trapped him leg-before as he played forward. His partnership with Aneesh yielded 105 runs, blending aggression with caution. Aneesh, who had looked well set, soon followed, miscuing a short ball from Parvez Sultan to Sandip at midwicket. Skipper Shreyas Gopal (19) was bowled by Sultan, while KL Shrijith (13), who had begun to find his rhythm with a classic sweep for six off Sandip, offered a regulation catch to Bikram Das at cover off Abhijith. Aneeshwar Gautam (33 batting) and Manvanth Kumar (6 batting) saw off the remaining overs, with the latter striking two sixes over long-on and midwicket. While the advantage still firmly rests with Karnataka, the next two days will be about how they can turn into a much-needed victory. SCOREBOARD Tripura (I innings): 194. Karnat

item.title: 2027 Dakar Rally To Be Moved Out Of Saudi Arabia
item.description: New location to be announced soon Photos by Edo Bauer. Dakar Rally organizers announced the 2027 competition will not be run in Saudi Arabia due to security concerns. The 2027 Dakar Rally is currently scheduled for January 1-15, but with the region currently sustaining strikes from Iran-backed Houthi rebels, the Amaury Sport Organisation (ASO) and Saudi Motorsport Company (SMC) decided to be proactive and move the event to a new host territory to be announced in the coming days. The Fédération Internationale de l'Automobile (FIA) and the Fédération Internationale de Motocyclisme (FIM) have both backed the move. The ASO and SMC described the decision as "exceptional and one-off," and Saudi Arabia is still slated to host Dakar in 2028, which would mark the Rally's 50th edition. Both organizations say they are already working together on that milestone. The ASO, a privately-owned French company that also runs the Tour de France and the World Rally Raid Championship, will remain the organizer of the 2027 Dakar Rally, wherever it will take place. The ASO says it is working directly with competitors, teams and partners to manage the transition, which is important as a lot of the logistics for Saudi Arabia have already been arranged. Where the rally goes next is the open question for everyone building bikes and plotting logistics around it. According to various reports in the Spanish media, one preferred option is to start the Dakar Rally in Spain and finish in Morocco, which would return the event to African soil for the first time since 2007. The Dakar Rally is no stranger to making changes due to security concerns. The event originally began in 1978 as a rally from Paris, France, to Dakar, Senegal. From 1992 to 2007, the route made some modifications, and did not always start in Paris or end at Dakar. The 2008 Dakar Rally was called off a day before the intended start, following a Christmas Eve attack in Mauritania that killed four French tourists. Escalating security concerns in North Africa led to the Dakar Rally's move to South America from 2009 to 2019, before the Rally moved to Saudi Arabia in 2020. Become a Motorcycle.com insider. item.title: How long will Jaren Jackson Jr., Lauri Markkanen be out of the Jazz lineup?
item.description: Utah Jazz forward Jaren Jackson Jr. (20) shoots a layup during a game against the Los Angeles Lakers at the Delta Center in Salt Lake City on Sunday, Oct. 25, 2026. | Lukas Katilius, Deseret News The Utah Jazz gave an update on two of their top players one day after Jaren Jackson Jr. and Lauri Markkanen both left the team’s 110-105 loss to the Memphis Grizzlies on Monday. item.title: Real Madrid star sends congratulations to Harry Kane on Ballon d’Or win
item.description: Real Madrid star sends congratulations to Harry Kane on Ballon d’Or win Real Madrid star Jude Bellingham has taken to social media, to send a message of congratulations the way of fellow countryman Harry Kane. This of course comes fresh off a special night for the Bayern Munich goalscorer on Monday. After making the trip back to his home country of England for the 2026 Ballon d’Or ceremony, Kane beat out the competition of La Liga pair Lamine Yamal and Kylian Mbappé to be named world football’s best player for the last 12 months. Messages of congratulations, in turn, have since come pouring in for the 33-year-old from across the world of football. And as alluded to above, amongst those to have sent his best Kane’s way was one of runner-up Kylian Mbappé’s teammates at Real Madrid. Having long shared a close bond with Kane on the international front, Jude Bellingham took to his official Instagram account, to write: ‘Congratulations, Skip!’ Conor Laird – GSFN

item.title: The next Dominik Szoboszlai is coming to join Andoni Iraola's first-team soon
item.description: The next Dominik Szoboszlai is coming to join Andoni Iraola's first-team soon There's a new Dominik Szoboszlai at Liverpool and he's coming to join Andoni Iraola's first-team soon. Liverpool's Hungarian midfield maestro has become a fan favourite over the last few years. Szoboszlai's terrific goals and incredible work-rate have made him an essential player for the Reds. Having spent over three years at Liverpool and penned a new long-term contract until 2031, Szoboszlai is also the future face of the club. With captain's Virgil van Dijk's contract expiring at the end of the season and vice captains Alisson's and Joe Gomez's contract also expiring, Szoboszlai is a prime candidate to wear the armband. He is already a vice captain and he has been captaining his nation for a long time. There's nobody more deserving of the recognition than the Reds' no.8. Andoni Iraola's working his magic at Liverpool In the absence of Szoboszlai, who has been suffering from a hamstring injury, it's a credit to the Reds' Spaniard that that the club has been able to maintain its form. Iraola was hired by Liverpool because of his ability to maximise his players' potential. We're already seeing the fruits of his exciting labour. Youngsters like Lewis Koumas and Trey Nyoni have stepped up and delivered when needed. Rio Ngumoha already looks a class above compared to last season. Ultimately, everyone is playing with confidence again, which is the most important part. Liverpool are finally back to the way they were playing and operating under Jurgen Klopp, and that means there are more opportunities for other young players to make their mark. Ollie O'Connor will be coming to Liverpool's first-team soon One of the best traits that Szoboszlai possesses is his versatility. Last season, Szoboszlai played as a right-back, and he played very well in that role. Over the course of his career at Anfield Szoboszlai has been used on the wing, he has played as a no.9 and as a no.10 while also playing deeper as a no.6 and naturally playing his more comfortable no.8 position. The Hungarian can simply play anywhere, and Liverpool look to be producing a player very similar to him in that regard. During his career at Liverpool, Ollie O'Connor has played on the wing, in midfield, and more recently, he's been used as a right-back for the club's U21 side. Like Szoboszlai, he is a tenacious player with a great work-ethic and strong technical tools. The youngster has three assists in 11 games from right-back this season, including two in his last two games for the U21s. He has been the Reds' best-performing player at U21 level, and given the lack of depth in the right-back and midfield departments, O'Connor looks next in line to join Iraola's first-team and earn a promotion. So, it's worth keeping a close eye on him.

item.title: Harrison Butker Addresses His Dismal Start to Chiefs Season as Coach Andy Reid Says He Needs to ‘Fix It’
item.description: Harrison Butker on Aug. 15, 2026 Credit: David Eulitt/Getty NEED TO KNOW Harrison Butker addressed his poor play this season after missing two field goals in the Chiefs’ 20-3 loss to the Seahawks “It’s kind of the life of a kicker — it either goes in or it doesn’t, and unfortunately, there’s been some kicks that haven’t gone in,” Butker said Head coach Andy Reid said Butker’s “got to fix it” Chiefs kicker Harrison Butker is struggling this season, and head coach Andy Reid is looking for a solution. After the 31-year-old Chief missed two field goal attempts in their crushing 20-3 loss to the Seattle Seahawks on Sunday, Oct. 25, Butker spoke to reporters about his continually disappointing performance this season. “I try to take one kick at a time,” said Butker, who started making headlines for more than his play in May 2024 when he told college graduates to “fight against the cultural emasculation of men” in a commencement speech. Harrison Butker on Sept. 20, 2026 Credit: Scott Winters/Icon Sportswire via Getty Butker continued, “I’m blessed every opportunity I get and try to do my best. It’s kind of the life of a kicker — it either goes in or it doesn’t, and unfortunately, there’s been some kicks that haven’t gone in.” Just before halftime of the Chiefs vs. Seahawks, Butker missed a 58-yard field goal when Seattle was up 10-0. Of that miss, Butker said it was “just short” after the game. He added, “Otherwise it was [in the] middle. Obviously, you want to make it, but it was short. And then the 40-yarder at the end, you just got to make it. Just pushed it.” He missed a second field goal against Seattle in the fourth quarter that would have put the Chiefs within just one touchdown and an extra point away from tying the game. Butker’s field goal percentage this season is just 68.8% and puts him at fourth-worst in the NFL. Reid addressed Butker’s struggles after their loss to the Seahawks on Sunday. “He’s been one of the most consistent kickers in football, but he’s off a bit, so we’ve got to fix it,” Reid told reporters. Quarterback Patrick Mahomes couldn’t seem to get the Chiefs into the game, going 19 for 33 for 165 yards, plus an interception . It was the worst statistical performance of the three-time Super Bowl champion’s career. item.title: UCF Space Game week is here. How it became football tradition with cool uniforms
item.description: The Space Game has reached Year 10. The 10th mission launches Friday with the UCF Knights transforming into the Citronauts against the Baylor Bears . Of course, they'll wear themed uniforms , which were unveiled in September. Kickoff is set for 7:30 p.m. at the Acrisure Bounce House. ESPN will broadcast the contest. "I think it's cool," head coach Scott Frost said. "There's so many neat aspects to UCF and where we came from and what we stand for and things that other schools don't have. I like how we're pouring into that and doubling down on that. Coming off the win we had ( over previous No. 2 BYU last Saturday) and the fact that it's the Space Game, I hope there's a ton of fans." UCF will hope to regain some of its extraterrestrial magic. Last year, the Knights lost the Space Game for the first time since its 2017 inception. Here's a breakdown on the 2026 edition and the history behind it. When is UCF Space Game 2026? UCF will host Baylor on Oct. 30. It's the second straight season the Knights have played on a Friday night with a nationally televised audience. Why does UCF football have a Space Game tradition? Since 2017, UCF has commemorated its roots as a school — then known as Florida Technological University — founded with the goal of providing personnel for the United States space program at Kennedy Space Center and Cape Canaveral Air Force Station. According to university statistics, 29% of Kennedy Space Center employees are UCF alumni. UCF offers more than 35 space-related degrees, including aerospace medicine and an online space MBA. UCF faculty and students have worked on 591 NASA projects to the 1990s. The Acrisure Bounce House's 50-yard line aligns on the exact latitude as Launch Complex 39A, NASA's most historic launchpad, 31 miles east. Rocket launches are frequently visible from the stands and press box inside the stadium. What is a Citronaut? Old UCF mascot has cult following According to Pegasus, the university's magazine, the Citronaut graced the cover of Florida Technological University's 1968-69 student handbook. It had the head of an astronaut, including a space helmet, and the body of an orange. Norman Van Meter, the brother-in-law of then-UCF President Charles Millican, illustrated the mascot in an attempt to combine Central Florida's major themes of the period: the growing space program and the citrus industry. Both remain integral to the region to this day. The Citronaut, however, was met with initial disapproval from FTU students. Within one year, they petitioned student government to establish an official mascot, eventually choosing "the Knights of Pegasus" in 1970. UCF rebranded as the Golden Knights in 1993, and the moniker was shortened to Knights in 2007. Nowadays, the Citronaut enjoys a large cult following and is a wildly popular secondary brand for the university's athletic teams. What is UCF football record in Space Games? item.title: The crucial course-management mistake costing you strokes (and how to fix it)
item.description: Knowing your dispersion pattern can help you aim better on the course. Getty Images One of the biggest course-management mistakes I see golfers make is aiming at the flagstick without considering where their shots typically miss. I joke with my students during playing lessons that they aim at more flagsticks than I do, and I’m the professional! I encourage golfers to play aggressively to conservative targets. It might sound contradictory, but the concept is simple: choose a smart target, then make an aggressive, committed swing. To understand why this works, you need to recognize your shotgun pattern i.e. the dispersion of your shots around an intended target. Nobody hits every shot perfectly. Some miss left, some right, some short and some long. That’s why it’s crucial to pick a target that leaves even your bad shots in an OK spot. Understanding your predominant miss should influence where you aim. For example, if your typical miss is left and the flag is tucked on the left side of the green, aiming directly at the stick increases your chances of short-siding yourself. Aim toward the middle instead, and that same miss will leave you with a birdie putt. I demonstrated this during a playing lesson when I told a student I was aiming at a palm tree behind the middle of the green. The flag was on the right, but I knew my tendency was a slight pull. I made my swing, pulled the shot slightly and finished about three feet from the hole. Had my student not known my intended target, he would have assumed I’d aimed directly at the flag and executed a tremendous shot. But I hadn’t. I’d actually missed my target. My strategy simply allowed that miss to produce a great result. That’s the difference between good course management and relying on perfect execution. The next time you’re approaching a green, consider the trouble, your typical miss and where an imperfect shot might finish. If you do that, you’ll start shooting lower scores without changing anything about your swing. Remember: Conservative target. Aggressive swing. That should be your mantra on the course. item.title: Bednar Opens Up About Avalanche’s Inconsistent Play and Need for Urgency
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect As a team, the Colorado Avalanche have already seen through 12 games what they’re capable of when they’re engaged and executing at a high level. The problem is how quickly things fall apart when they aren’t. “We haven’t found any middle ground yet, really,” head coach Jared Bednar said at the Avalanche’s practice facility on Tuesday. “When it’s bad, it’s really bad.” Those were among the most telling comments from Bednar as the Avalanche returned to the ice following arguably their worst performance of the season. After losing consecutive games to the Philadelphia Flyers and New Jersey Devils last week, Colorado responded with a convincing 6-3 win over the Tampa Bay Lightning on Friday. But whatever progress the Avalanche made in that game disappeared two nights later in Nashville. They lost 6-2 to a struggling Predators team on the tail end of a back to back. It was embarrassing. Bednar’s frustrations aren’t just about the loss. It’s about how dramatically his team has swung between its best and worst performances, and how little consistency it’s shown through the opening weeks of the season. “The most important part of it is the urgency, because you can’t convince me that you go and play a game like Philly and then the next night in Jersey, which part of it I understand, and then you go and play like you do against Tampa, and then you go right back to the way you were,” Bednar said. “A lot of it is urgency and work ethic and competitiveness, and that’s what I’m seeing with our team. When we bring it and our execution’s high, we’re playing not just good, we’re playing really good. And then when we don’t bring that, I’ve noticed this year more than any other one, that when we’re not engaged, our execution is horrible, and we’re going nowhere.” The Avalanche have dealt with difficult starts before. Last season, they won just five of their first 10 games, despite several of those losing contests going to overtime. In 2023-24, goaltending and depth issues contributed to a 14-13-0 start through a third of the season. Even during the 2022-23 season, following their Stanley Cup championship, Colorado was 20-17-3 through 40 games and outside the playoff picture after a loss to the last-place Chicago Blackhawks. Each time, the Avalanche found a way to turn things around, ultimately winning at least 49 games in those seasons. There are reasons to believe they can do it again. But this year’s struggles have a different feel. Colorado isn’t dealing with the same level of goaltending uncertainty it faced two years ago, nor has it been forced to navigate the extensive lineup issues that plagued the team in 2022-23 and two years later when they dressed more than 50 skaters in the regular season. For the most part, the Avalanche have had their core players available but the inconsistencies have still persisted for a month. item.title: Buffalo Bills make defensive roster moves before Week 8 vs. Baltimore Ravens
item.description: CLEVELAND, OHIO - DECEMBER 21: Andre Jones Jr. #75 of the Buffalo Bills waits for the snap during the third quarter against the Cleveland Browns at Huntington Bank Field on December 21, 2025 in Cleveland, Ohio. (Photo by Nick Cammett/Diamond Images via Getty Images) | Diamond Images/Getty Images The Buffalo Bills continue playing roster gymnastics with a core group of practice squad players in an effort to fine-tune their defensive needs week to week. In the lead-up to their Week 8 game against the Baltimore Ravens, Buffalo has re-signed outside linebacker Andre Jones Jr. and cornerback A.J. Woods to the team’s practice squad. To make room for Jones and Woods on the practice squad, the Bills released cornerback Anthony Kendall and defensive lineman Austin Johnson. Jones makes his way back to One Bills Drive after a short stint playing in three games this season with the Miami Dolphins. Jones played in three regular-season games for Buffalo during the 2025 NFL season, making five tackles (one solo). He appeared in one playoff game last season, registering one additional tackle (all stats per Pro Football Reference ). Kendall departs the Bills after playing 31 defensive snaps on defense during Buffalo’s road win over the Los Angeles Rams. His replacement, Woods, has yet to play in an NFL regular-season since becoming a pro in 2024. The 32-year-old Johnson has had several stints with the Bills, dating back to the 2024 NFL season in which he made two interceptions in the regular season for Buffalo’s defense. In total that season, Johnson played in 15 games, making one start; adding 19 tackles (7 solo), one quarterback hit, half a sack, two pass defenses, and the two aforementioned interceptions for nine yards (per Pro Football Reference ). item.title: Pundit Slams Former Rangers Captain And Legend: Was His Departure Right For The Club?
item.description: Pundit Slams Former Rangers Captain And Legend: Was His Departure Right For The Club? Rangers have started a new chapter under Derek McInnes after a summer of major squad changes, with a strong recent form (barring one blip) restoring belief in their Scottish Premiership title challenge. Back-to-back victories over Celtic have strengthened that momentum, while the 4-0 win against St Johnstone showed the side’s improved defensive organisation. item.title: Atlético learn their group and format for the 2027 Mineiro
item.description: Atlético learn their group and format for the 2027 Mineiro Atlético learned its group lineup and the new format for the 2027 Campeonato Mineiro on Tuesday (27). The decisions were made during the Technical Council meeting held by the Minas Gerais Football Federation (FMF) at Mineirão in Belo Horizonte, with representatives from all 12 participating clubs. The most successful club in the state championship, with 50 titles, Galo will be the top seed in Group A , alongside Pouso Alegre, North, Tombense, Betim and Villa Nova. The main change for 2027 will be the division of the 12 teams into two groups of six. In the first stage, clubs will face only opponents from the other group, playing each once for a total of six rounds. This means Atlético will face Cruzeiro, América, URT, Uberlândia, Minas do Sul (currently Itabirito) and Democrata de Sete Lagoas in the qualifying stage. New competition format The top four teams in each group will advance to the quarterfinals. From that stage onward, ties will be played over two legs, home and away. Another change will be the return of a two-legged final. Unlike in 2026, when the title was decided in a single match, the 2027 final will also feature home and away legs. The two teams with the worst overall records will be relegated to Módulo II. The FMF has set January 6 as the start date for the 2027 Campeonato Mineiro, with the competition scheduled to conclude on March 7 . The Federation will release the detailed fixture list, including dates, kickoff times and venues, at a later date. See the 2027 Mineiro groups Group A • Atlético • Pouso Alegre • North • Tombense • Betim • Villa Nova Group B • Cruzeiro • América • URT • Uberlândia • Minas do Sul (currently Itabirito) • Democrata-SL Other rule changes The Technical Council also approved changes to the competition rules for next season. • No limit on player registrations; • Yellow cards reset after the first stage; • Increase from six to eight coaching staff members on the bench; • Reduction of the minimum interval between matches from 66 to 63 hours; • Standardized pitch watering; • Introduction of hydration breaks in line with FIFA guidelines; • Option for visiting clubs to inspect stadiums. Atlético will enter the competition seeking its 51st Campeonato Mineiro title , further cementing its status as the most successful club in the state championship’s history. item.title: How did ‘Clutch City' become an iconic Houston nickname? Thank the Houston Chronicle.
item.description: By the time the Rockets beat the Suns in Game 5 of their second-round series, fans had adopted the "Clutch City" moniker. (Tim Johnson/Associated Press) Join us on a journey to better understand Houston, one question at a time. Sign up to get the Houston Explained newsletter in your inbox every Tuesday and Friday. W ith time running out in the Rockets' matchup against the Spurs last Friday in Austin, San Antonio superstar Victor Wembanyama was inches away from tying the game. But Houston's Amen Thompson met him at the rim, leapt to the heavens (for Wembanyama is, respectfully, freakishly tall) and swatted Wemby's layup away to seal the win. Watching and rewatching that now-viral moment , which a Spurs player described as "one out of a million," I was reminded of the photo at the top of this newsletter, and the nickname Houston basketball fans have embraced since the Rockets' 1994 championship run: Clutch City. I was not yet a Houstonian, nor was I even born, when the moniker was impressed into the city's sporting history, but I have lived here long enough to know that Houston truly embodies it, on and off the court. So I started digging into how the name came to be, and I found that Clutch City owes its existence, at least in part, to an infamous two-word headline the newspaper I work for splashed across the first page of its sports section in May 1994 . One that called the city something far less flattering. 'Choke City' The headline ran on May 12, 1994, the morning after the Rockets blew a 20-point fourth-quarter lead in Game 2 of the Western Conference semifinals against the Phoenix Suns at The Summit (now Lakewood Church). The phrase "Choke City" was first written by longtime Chronicle sports columnist Fran Blinebury, and the name ran in the Chronicle's sports section in bold letters. Harsh as it was, it wasn't entirely wrong. Houston sports fans had spent years watching their teams fall apart in big moments. There was, of course, the Oilers' painful loss to the Buffalo Bills in 1993, when Houston squandered a 35-3 lead and lost in overtime . And the Rockets themselves had been knocked out in overtime of a Game 7 in Seattle the year prior. So when the Rockets let a big lead slip away in Game 1 of the Suns series, too, and then lost again at home in Game 2, fans seemed to know exactly how the story would end. Making matters worse, after Game 1, Rockets guard Vernon Maxwell had called out fans for not filling The Summit. "Our fans are the worst," Maxwell told reporters. "And you can write that. Tell them I said that. To hell with them." Rockets fans packed the arena for Game 2, only to watch it happen all over again. The memorable "Choke City" headline from May 12, 1994, after the Rockets blew a 20-point fourth quarter lead to lose Game 2 of the Western Conference semifinals to the Suns was the product of years of Houston sports frustration. As Aikman has spent recent weeks coming to terms with the possibility that ESPN and Buck might be ready to move on without him, the former Dallas Cowboys quarterback expressed interest in returning to the franchise he won three Super Bowls with. I don’t know of anyone in any part of football that’s had more success off the field than Troy. He is a successful guy. item.description: | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Tony Siracusa, CFB Managing Editor Wake Forest is done resting for the season, and it is time to refocus. After a bye week, the Demon Deacons are 6-1 overall and 4-1 in the conference with five games left in the season. They are home Saturday against the Virginia Cavaliers, who come into Winston-Salem 4-4 overall and 2-3 in conference play. So how did Wake Forest spend its time off after the win at Cal? A mix of rest, recuperation, and self-evaluation. The Wake Forest Refocus “It was huge. It was really huge,” head coach Jake Dickert said on Monday when talking about having the time to get some rest in after seven straight games to open the season. After the Cal game , there were no official practices until this last Thursday. That gave the players time to heal any of the aches, pains, and minor injuries that hampered them. Receiver Carlos Hernandez managed only a few snaps in the Cal game due to a nagging injury, so the time to rehab was particularly big for him. “There’s a ton of guys, especially on the defensive line of scrimmage that were playing with a lot of little things.” The time off was also spent doing a lot of internal scouting. Dickert said there were meetings with the players about where they need to be going forward in order to maintain the success they have had to this point. “You’re not watching it with a warm, fuzzy feeling,” Dickert said of the game film reviews that went on during the break. “You’ve got to look at it with a real eye, to say, ‘Where can we really improve? Where are our tendencies at?’ I can go into a million different things.” That evaluation goes beyond the players and to the coaching staff and Dickert himself. “We identified some failed techniques. We’ve got to get the pads back on, especially with our offensive line and defensive line, and we’ve got to do better at it.” We asked Dickert what a self-evaluation of his work so far this season looked like. He said it included getting feedback from the players. The result, he said, is to make sure he is the same coach from one day to the next. “At the end of the day, it’s just be ultra consistent,” he said. “I can’t be walking around here like every day is fourth and one. We’ve got to be able to do the things consistently that we did to generate this type of success. I think that starts with me.” He said the daily routines and the way the coaches are delivering their messages to the players are key. “At the end of the day, if you put in more time because you perceive any game as more important, you’re already wrong.” Photo courtesy: Jaylynn Nash-Imagn Images The Coaching Rumors To that point, Dickert said he is spending no time on the outside noise involving his name and college football coaching openings.
